DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Control System Inputs

 A/C Ambient Air Temperature Sensor 

The A/C ambient air temperature sensor and bracket (19E702):

is located in front of the A/C condenser core (19712) near the center 
of the vehicle.

contains a thermistor which measures the temperature of outside air as 
a resistance and sends that reading to the electronic automatic temperature 
control assembly.

 In-Car Temperature Sensor 

The in-car temperature sensor, which is part of the message center 
control panel, operates in the following manner:

A thermistor in the in-car temperature sensor measures air temperature 
inside the passenger compartment.

An automatic temperature control sensor hose and elbow (19D888) is 
connected between the A/C evaporator housing (19850) and the in-car 
temperature sensor.

The automatic temperature control sensor hose and elbow takes air from 
the A/C evaporator housing air stream to create a suction in the in-car 
temperature sensor.

The suction draws in-vehicle air into the in-car temperature sensor and 
across the thermistor.

 A/C Sunload Sensor 

The A/C sunload sensor (19E663):

is located on the top RH side of the instrument panel (04320) above the 
glove compartment (06010).

contains a photovoltaic diode that is sensitive to light.

has some unspecified resistance across the terminals depending upon the 
amount of light reaching the photovoltaic diode, therefore the only test that 
can be performed is for an internal short circuit.

 A/C Cycling Switch 

The A/C cycling switch (19E561) is mounted on a Schrader valve-type 
fitting on the top of the suction accumulator/drier (19C836).

A valve depressor, located inside the threaded end of the A/C cycling 
switch, presses in on the Schrader valve stem.

This allows the suction pressure inside the suction accumulator/drier 
to control the operation of the A/C cycling switch. 

The electrical switch contacts open when the suction pressure drops to 
152-193 kPa (22-28 psi). 

The contacts close when the suction pressure rises to 276-324 kPa 
(40-47 psi). 

When the A/C cycling switch contacts close, the signal to energize the 
A/C clutch (2884) is sent to the powertrain control module through the 
electronic automatic temperature control module.

When the A/C cycling switch contacts open, the A/C clutch field coil 
(2987) is deenergized and compressor operation stops. 

The A/C cycling switch will control the A/C evaporator core pressure at 
a point where the plate/fin surface temperature will be maintained slightly 
above freezing.

This prevents icing of the A/C evaporator core (19860) and blockage of 
airflow. 

It is not necessary to discharge the refrigerant system to remove the 
A/C cycling switch.

 A/C Pressure Transducer 

The A/C pressure transducer is mounted on a Schrader valve-type fitting 
on the A/C compressor to condenser discharge line (19972).

A valve depressor, located inside the threaded end of the A/C pressure 
transducer, presses in on the Schrader valve stem.

This allows the compressor discharge pressure to be monitored by the 
powertrain control module.

The A/C pressure transducer provides a voltage signal that is 
proportional to the A/C compressor discharge pressure.

The powertrain control module uses this information for A/C clutch 
control, cooling fan control and idle speed control.

It is not necessary to discharge the refrigerant system to remove the 
A/C pressure transducer.

Section 412-04: Control Components

1997 Mark VIII Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Control System Outputs

 A/C Blower Motor Speed Control 

The A/C blower motor speed control (19E624) is located under the A/C 
evaporator housing (19850), forward of the blower motor (18527). 

The function of the A/C blower motor speed control is to convert low 
power signals from the electronic automatic temperature control assembly to a 
high current, variable ground feed for the blower motor. 

A/C blower motor speed is infinitely variable and is controlled by the 
electronic automatic temperature control software.

A delay function provides a gradual increase or decrease in blower 
motor speed under all conditions. 

 A/C Electric Blend Door Actuator 

The A/C electric blend door actuator is located on the rear of the A/C 
evaporator housing.

Its function is to move the A/C air temperature control doors on 
command from the control assembly.

The A/C electric blend door actuator contains a reversible electric 
motor and a potentiometer. The potentiometer wiper is connected to the 
actuator output shaft and moves with the output shaft to indicate the position 
of the A/C air temperature control door.

A 5 volt signal is applied to the ends of the potentiometer. The 
voltage available at the wiper indicates the position of the potentiometer. 
The expressed value of the actuator wiper voltage is sent to the electronic 
automatic temperature control module and is matched with the wiper voltage of 
the module potentiometer. The control module then drives the actuator motor in 
whichever direction is necessary to make the actuator wiper voltage agree with 
the control module wiper voltage.

 Vacuum Control Motors 

The vacuum control motors (18A318):

are located on the A/C evaporator housing, A/C recirculating air duct 
(19C590) and heater air plenum chamber (18471).

direct system airflow to the vehicle interior as determined by the 
electronic automatic temperature control module or manual override.

 Variable Load Control Module 

The variable load control module:

is located behind the RH front wheel inner splash shield.

incorporates circuit control provisions for the fan motor (8C607) and 
the A/C clutch field coil (2987). 

communicates with the powertrain control module through the multiplex 
communication network.

A/C Clutch ON

 a The A/C clutch circuit is energized by the EATC module but
the final control of clutch operation is determined by the powertrain control
module through the variable load control module. The A/C clutch can be shut
off (or kept off) for several seconds at engine start-up, during high engine
speeds, during acceleration, during low engine idle conditions (approximately
200 rpm below idle specs) and when the engine coolant temperature sensor
reading exceeds approximately 120°C (248°F).

 b If the engine coolant temperature fails to reach 50°C
(122°F) after 3 1/2 minutes of operation, the heater blower motor speed
will increase and the windshield defroster door will shift from defrost
position to floor position.

The transmission range indicator:

1997 Mark VIII

Section 413-01: Instrument Cluster

1997 Mark VIII Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Warning Indicators

 Charging System 

The charging system indicator:

is controlled by the voltage regulator in the generator.

is displayed when the voltage regulator pulls the line low due to a 
charging system concern.

is displayed with ignition switch in run or start (with engine off) and 
will go out when generator starts to charge system.

 Low Oil Pressure 

The low oil pressure indicator:

is controlled by the engine oil pressure switch.

is displayed when the oil pressure switch closes to ground due to 
insufficient oil pressure.

has a 3-second prove out on engine start up.

 Brake System 

The brake system indicator:

has a 3-second prove out on start up.

is displayed when brake fluid level is low.

is displayed when parking brake engaged data message is received over 
the J1850 Communications Network from the steering column/ignition/lighting 
control module.

defaults to on if communication is lost to the steering 
column/ignition/lighting control module.

 Anti-Lock Brake (ABS) Warning Indicator 

The anti-lock brake (ABS) warning indicator:

receives on or off data over the J1850 Communications Network from the 
anti-lock brake (ABS) control module.

is displayed if communication is lost to the anti-lock brake (ABS) 
control module.

is displayed when there is a concern in the ABS.

is displayed if the odometer rolling count is not received from the 
anti-lock brake (ABS) control module.

has a 3-second prove out on engine start up.

 High Beam 

The high beam indicator:

is wired to the high beam headlamp circuitry, controlled by the 
steering column/ignition/lighting control module.

is displayed when the high beam headlamps are on.

 LH/RH Turn Signals 

The LH/RH turn signal indicator:

is wired to the respective turn signal circuitry, and controlled by the 
steering column/ignition/lighting control module.

flashes at a faster rate to alert driver of a bulb outage condition.

are wired to an internal relay within the hybrid electronic instrument 
cluster which provides the audible clicking noise when operating.

 Speed Control 

The speed control indicator:

is controlled by the speed control module.

is displayed only when speed control is set and operating.

 Traction Control (If Equipped) 

The traction control indicator:

has a 3-second prove out on engine start up.

receives traction control active data over the J1850 Communications 
Network from the ABS module.

is displayed only when the traction control is in operation.

is displayed if communication is lost to the anti-lock brake (ABS) 
control module.

 Inspection and Verification 

Verify the customer's concern by operating the instrument cluster 
(10849) to duplicate the condition by observing the indicators and gauges to 
determine if they are operating properly with the ignition switch:

in RUN with the engine off.

in START before the ignition switch is released.

in RUN with the engine running.

Inspect to determine if any of the following mechanical or electrical 
concerns apply.

 Visual Inspection Chart

Mechanical

Electrical

Engine coolant level

Accessory drive belt

Engine oil level

Brake fluid level

Damaged fuse: fuse junction panel

Fuse 20 (10A)

Fuse 17 (10A)

Fuse 5 (10A)

Fuse 28 (10A)

Circuit wiring

Switches or sensors

If the inspection reveals obvious concern(s) that can be readily 
identified, service as required.

If the concern remains after the inspection, connect the Rotunda New 
Generation Star (NGS) Tester to the data link connector (DLC) located beneath 
the instrument panel to perform DATA LINK DIAGNOSTIC TEST; refer to Section 418-00 
. If the NGS responds with NO 
RESPONSE/NOT EQUIPPED for the hybrid electronic instrument cluster, go to Pinpoint Test A 
. 
If the NGS responds with NO RESPONSE/NOT EQUIPPED for the 
steering column/ignition/lighting control module, go to Pinpoint Test B 
. If 
the DATA LINK DIAGNOSTIC TEST is passed for the hybrid electronic instrument 
cluster and the steering column/ignition/lighting control module, retrieve 
continuous diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs) and execute Self Test Diagnostics 
for the hybrid electronic instrument cluster and the steering 
column/ignition/lighting control module; refer to Section 418-00 
.

If the self test is passed and no diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs) are 
retrieved, go to the Symptom Chart 

to continue diagnostics.

If DTCs are retrieved for the hybrid electronic instrument cluster, go 
to the Hybrid Electronic Instrument Cluster (HEC) Diagnostic Trouble Code 
(DTC) Index to continue diagnostics. If DTCs are retrieved for the steering 
column/ignition/lighting control module, go to the Steering 
Column/Ignition/Lighting Control (SCIL) Module Diagnostic Trouble Code (DTC) 
Index to continue diagnostics.

If the hybrid electronic instrument cluster cannot be accessed by the 
NGS tester, go to Pinpoint Test A 
. 
If the steering column/ignition/lighting 
control module cannot be accessed by the NGS tester, go to Pinpoint Test B 
.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Instrument Cluster

 Removal 

 NOTE: Federal law requires that the odometer in any replacement speedometer 
must register the same mileage as that registered on the removed 
speedometer/odometer. Service replacement speedometer/odometer and odometer 
modules with the same mileage preset to actual vehicle mileage are available 
through Ford electronic service centers. In nearly all instances, the mileage 
continues to accumulate in the odometer memory even if the odometer does not 
display mileage. This mileage can usually be verified by the electronic 
service centers. Contact the service center for instructions to receive a 
replacement speedometer/odometer or odometer module with the mileage preset to 
actual mileage. 

 NOTE: If the actual vehicle mileage cannot be verified, the service center 
will supply a speedometer/odometer module with the odometer display preset to 
zero ("0") miles and the service odometer segment ("s") illuminated in the 
vicinity of the odometer display. In addition, an odometer mileage sticker is 
supplied with the replacement odometer. This sticker must display the 
estimated vehicle mileage and is to be affixed to the driver door. 

 NOTE: The instrument cluster is serviced as an assembly; do not disassemble 
cluster.

Disconnect the battery ground cable (14301); refer to Section 414-01 
.

Lift the instrument panel defroster opening grille (044E82) high enough 
that retaining clips are above instrument panel.

[FIGURE: AK1350A.gif]

Remove the instrument panel finish panel (04339); refer to Section 501-12 
.

Remove the retaining screws from the instrument cluster (10N848).

[FIGURE: AK1351A.gif]

Rotate the bottom of the instrument cluster out first, disconnect the 
two electrical connectors and remove the instrument cluster.

[FIGURE: AK1352A.gif]

 Installation 

Follow removal procedure in reverse order.

[FIGURE: AK0051A.gif]

Section 413-08A: Driver Information/Message Center

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Message Center

[FIGURE: AK0353B.gif]

The message center consists of a message center indicator assembly and 
a message center switch module.

The message center includes the following modes of display:

FUEL COMPUTER AND TRIP ODOMETER

DRIVER SETTINGS MENU

VEHICLE SETTINGS MENU

AUTOLAMP DELAY TIME

SYSTEM CHECK

PERSONALITY STATUS MESSAGES

COMPASS DISPLAY

DATE AND TIME DISPLAY

PHONE DISPLAY (IF EQUIPPED)

WARNING AND STATUS MESSAGES

================================================================================
PAGE 4822
================================================================================
1997 Mark VIII

Section 413-08A: Driver Information/Message Center

1997 Mark VIII Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Fuel Computer and Trip Odometer

The fuel computer and trip odometer compute six functions. The RANGE, 
ECONOMY and TRIP ODOMETER switches are used to select and display:

AVERAGE FUEL ECONOMY

INSTANT FUEL ECONOMY

DISTANCE TO EMPTY (DTE)

FUEL REMAINING

TRIP 1 ODOMETER

TRIP 2 ODOMETER

 RANGE 

The RANGE switch controls the following displays:

Distance to empty (DTE)

Fuel Remaining

 ECONOMY 

The ECONOMY switch controls the following displays:

Average fuel economy

Instant fuel economy

 TRIP ODOMETER 

The TRIP ODOMETER switch controls the following displays:

Trip A odometer

Trip B odometer

The message center receives fuel computer and trip odometer data from 
the following modules:

fuel pump module

anti-lock brake control module

powertrain control module (PCM) (12A650).

1997 Mark VIII Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Driver Settings

The driver setting mode allows the driver to turn ON or OFF selected 
features by means of the reset switch. The driver setting switch controls:

Express window

Auto lock

Horn chirp

Easy entry/exit (seat and steering column)

Driver seat autoglide

Phone display (if equipped)

Reverse tilt mirrors

The message center indicator module receives/sends driver settings 
information to the following modules:

Driver seat module

Driver door module

Steering column/ignition/lighting control module.

Section 413-08A: Driver Information/Message Center

1997 Mark VIII Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Vehicle Settings

The vehicle setting mode allows the driver to display and turn ON or 
OFF selected vehicle features by means of the RESET switch, with the exception 
of the autolamps delay time display. The vehicle setting switch controls:

Traction control

English/metric display

Wipers/headlamp (ON or OFF)

Autolamps delay time (display only)

Oil life

The message center indicator module receives/sends Vehicle Settings 
information to the following modules:

anti-lock brake (ABS) control module

electronic automatic temperature control (EATC) module

steering column/ignition/lighting control module

powertrain control module (PCM)

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

System Check

The system check function provides the driver information on the 
current status of certain vehicle functions. By pressing the SYSTEM CHECK 
switch on the message center switch module (10D996), the following messages 
will be displayed in the message center:

 NOTE: The ignition switch must be in the RUN position for the air ride switch 
status, engine temp and traction control system status to be displayed during 
system check.

OIL LIFE OK, CHANGE OIL SOON or OIL CHANGE REQUIRED

Oil life left (in percent of life remaining)

LOW OIL LEVEL

VOLTAGE LEVEL OK or CHECK CHARGING SYSTEM

ENGINE TEMP OK or CHECK ENGINE TEMP

COOLANT LEVEL OK or LOW COOLANT LEVEL

WASHER FLUID LEVEL OK or LOW WASHER FLUID

DRIVER DOOR AJAR or DRIVER DOOR CLOSED

RIGHT DOOR AJAR or RIGHT DOOR CLOSED

TRUNK AJAR or TRUNK CLOSED

HEADLAMPS OK or CHECK HEADLAMPS

FRONT TURN LAMPS OK or CHECK FRONT TURN LAMPS

BRAKE LAMPS OK or CHECK BRAKE LAMPS

TAIL LAMPS OK or CHECK TAIL LAMPS

AIR RIDE SYSTEM OK, CHECK AIR RIDE SYSTEM or AIR RIDE SWITCH OFF

TRACTION CONTROL OK, CHECK TRACTION CONTROL or TRACTION CONTROL 
DISABLED (IF EQUIPPED)

FUEL LEVEL OK or LOW FUEL LEVEL

MILES TO EMPTY or KILOMETERS TO EMPTY

Section 413-08A: Driver Information/Message Center

1997 Mark VIII Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Warning Messages

System warnings alert the driver to possible concerns in the vehicle's 
operating systems. The message center indicator module will display all active 
warning messages for four seconds. The following messages will be displayed in 
the message center:

 Door Ajar Warnings 

RIGHT DOOR AJAR

Is displayed when the passenger door is open with the ignition switch 
in the RUN position and the steering column/ignition/lighting (SCIL) control 
module activates the message center indicator module through the J1850 
communication network.

DRIVER DOOR AJAR

When the driver door is opened with the ignition switch in the RUN 
position, the driver door module activates the message center through the 
J1850 communication network.

 Engine Coolant Temperature Warning 

When the engine temperature rises above a preset level, the powertrain 
control module (PCM) activates the message center indicator module CHECK 
ENGINE TEMP display through the J1850 communication network.

 Oil Level Warning 

 NOTE: If the vehicle is parked on a steep incline, the LOW OIL LEVEL warning 
may come on when the vehicle is started, even though the oil is at the correct 
level. The oil level is monitored while the engine is off, so the oil can 
drain into the oil pan to be measured. Some after-market devices such as 
remote starters if improperly installed, can cause the engine to start without 
alerting the oil monitoring system. This may also cause the LOW OIL LEVEL 
warning to come on when the vehicle is started, even though the oil is at the 
correct level.

When the engine oil level is low, the low oil level sensor activates 
the message center indicator module LOW OIL LEVEL warning.

 Brake Lamps Out Warning 

 NOTE: The center high mount stoplamp is not monitored.

When a stoplamp bulb is out, the steering column/ignition/lighting 
(SCIL) control module activates the message center indicator module CHECK 
BRAKE LAMPS display.

 Charging System Warning 

When there is a concern with the charging system, the battery charging 
circuit activates the message center indicator module CHECK CHARGING SYSTEM 
display.

 Fuel Level Warning 

When the distance to empty is less than 80 km (50 miles the message 
center indicator module displays LOW FUEL LEVEL display.

 Engine Coolant Level Warning 

When the engine coolant level is low, the engine coolant level sensor 
activates the message center indicator module LOW ENGINE COOLANT display.

 Headlamps Out Warning 

When a low beam headlamp bulb is out, the steering 
column/ignition/lighting (SCIL) control module activates the message center 
indicator module CHECK HEADLAMPS display through the J1850 communication 
network.

 Tail Lamps Out Warning 

When a tail lamp is out, the steering column/ignition/lighting (SCIL) 
control module activates the message center indicator module CHECK TAIL LAMPS 
display through the J1850 communication network.

 Front Turn Lamps Out Warning 

When a front turn signal lamp is out, the steering 
column/ignition/lighting (SCIL) activates the message center indicator module 
CHECK FRT TURN LAMPS display through the J1850 communication network.

 Washer Fluid Level Warning 

When the windshield washer fluid is low, the windshield washer fluid 
level sensor activates the message center indicator module LOW WASHER FLUID 
display.

 Luggage Compartment Door Ajar (TRUNK AJAR) Warning 

When the luggage compartment door is open with the ignition switch in 
RUN, the steering column/ignition/lighting (SCIL) control module activates the 
message center indicator module TRUNK AJAR display through the J1850 
communication network.

 Traction Control Warnings (If Equipped) 

CHECK TRACTION CONTROL

Is displayed when there is a concern with the traction control system 
detected by the anti-lock brake system/traction control (ABS/TC) module which 
activates the message center indicator module through the J1850 communication 
network.

TRACTION CONTROL DISABLED

Is displayed when the traction control is temporarily disabled due to 
an overheating condition, the anti-lock brake system/traction control (ABS/TC) 
module activates the message center indicator module through the J1850 
communication network.

 Air Suspension Service Switch Warning 

When the air suspension service switch is turned OFF, the air 
suspension service switch activates the message center AIR RIDE SWITCH OFF 
display.

 Air Suspension System Warning 

When there is an air suspension system concern detected by the 
steering/suspension module (SSM) it activates the message center CHECK AIR 
RIDE SYSTEM display.

 Oil Life Warning 

The engine oil level temperature sensor, the anti-lock brake (ABS) 
control module, odometer data and the powertrain control module rpm data are 
used by the message center indicator module to calculate oil life.

The message center indicator module displays:

CHANGE OIL SOON when engine oil life reaches five percent.

OIL CHANGE REQUIRED when engine oil life reaches zero percent.

 Data Error Warnings 

ENGINE TEMP DATA ERR

Is displayed when the powertrain control module (PCM) detects a concern 
with the engine temperature sensor and activates the message center indicator 
module through the J1850 communication network, or the message center 
indicator module does not receive the engine temperature data from the 
powertrain control module (PCM).

GEAR DISPLAY DATA ERR

Is displayed when a gear display data error is detected by the hybrid 
electronic cluster (HEC) and activates the message center indicator module 
through the J1850 communication network.

 Transmission Warnings 

CHECK TRANSMISSION

Is displayed when an internal transmission fault is detected by the 
powertrain control module (PCM) which activates the message center indicator 
module through the J1850 communication network.

TRANSMISSION OVERHEAT

Is displayed when the transmission fluid temperature rises above a 
preset level, monitored by the powertrain control module (PCM) which activates 
the message center indicator module through the J1850 communication network.

 Special Service Tool(s)

[FIGURE: ST1217A.gif]

New Generation Star (NGS) Tester

 Inspection and Verification 

Verify the customer's concern by operating the message center indicator 
module to duplicate the condition.

Inspect to determine if one of the following mechanical or electrical 
concerns apply:

 Visual Inspection Chart

Mechanical

Electrical

Engine coolant level.

Engine oil level.

Windshield washer fluid level.

Damaged Fuse Junction Panel Fuse 20 (10A), Fuse 4 (10A).

Damaged switches/sensors.

Circuitry open/shorted.

If inspection reveals obvious concerns that can be readily identified, 
service as required.

If the concern remains after inspection, connect the Rotunda New 
Generation Star (NGS) Tester to the data link connector (DLC) located beneath 
the instrument panel to perform the DATA LINK DIAGNOSTIC TEST; refer to Section 418-00 
. If the New Generation Star (NGS) 
Tester responds with NO RESPONSE/NOT EQUIPPED for message center indicator 
module, go to Pinpoint Test B 
. 
If the DATA LINK DIAGNOSTIC TEST is passed for 
the message center indicator module, retrieve continuous diagnostic trouble 
codes (DTCs) and execute Self Test Diagnostics for message center indicator 
module; refer to Section 418-00 
.

If diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs) are retrieved, go to the Message 
Center Indicator Module Diagnostic Trouble Code (DTC) Index to continue 
diagnostics.

If the Message Center Indicator Module cannot be accessed by the New 
Generation Star (NGS) Tester, go to Pinpoint Test B 
.

If self-test is passed and no Diagnostic Trouble Codes (DTCs) are 
retrieved, perform the Message Center Indicator Module On-Board Diagnostic Test:

ROM Level and Checksum Test

EEPROM Level and Checksum Test

Display Test.

If the message center indicator module passes the on-board diagnostic 
tests, go to the Symptom Chart 

to continue diagnostics.

 Message Center Indicator Module On-Board Diagnostics Tests 

To perform message center indicator module on-board diagnostic test:

Press RANGE and COMPASS switches while turning the ignition switch from 
OFF to RUN.

Press the RANGE switch to advance the message center indicator module 
to the next test group.

Cycle the ignition from RUN to OFF and back to RUN to return to normal 
operation.

 ROM Level and Checksum Test 

This test displays the Read Only Memory level of the message center 
indicator module. It also displays a Read Only Memory Test checksum. The Read 
Only Memory checksum display (CHK), must display 00. If it is not 00, replace 
the message center indicator module.

 EEPROM Level and Checksum Test 

This test displays the Electrically Erasable Programmable Read Only 
Memory (EEPROM) level of the message center indicator module. It also displays 
an EEPROM Test checksum. The EEPROM checksum display (CHK), must display 0000. 
If it is not 0000, replace the message center indicator module.

 Display Test 

This test displays the same character in all 24 character positions. 
The initial character is all dots. Press the VEHICLE SETTINGS or TRIP ODO 
buttons to sequence through the entire character set. Replace the message 
center indicator module if characters are not displayed properly.

 Lamp Test 

This test lights each one of the warning indicators that the Message 
Center Indicator Module drives (FASTEN SAFETY BELT, O/D OFF, and TRACTION 
CONTROL OFF) in sequence. To sequence through the indicators, press the TRIP 
ODO button.

Test 1 illuminates fasten safety belt indicator.

Tests 2-6 are inactive and produce no output.

Test 7 illuminates the traction control off indicator.

Test 8 illuminates the O/D off indicator.

These tests can be used with the corresponding pinpoint tests to verify 
if the Message Center is working properly if a New Generation Star (NGS) 
Tester is not available and the pinpoint tests requires the indicator to be 
commanded on.

 Final Date 

This is a coded date that indicates when the message center indicator 
module was manufactured. This number is used when requesting assistance from 
the hotline.

 Serial Number 

This unique serial number is assigned during manufacturing. This number 
is used when requesting assistance from the hotline.

 A/D Channel Tests 

The following tests display the status of each of the analog inputs to 
the message center indicator module. To sequence through the different A/D 
tests, press the VEHICLE SETTINGS button to sequence forward, and the TRIP ODO 
button to sequence backward. Refer to A/D Input Table for the analog inputs 
associated with each test. These tests can be used with the pinpoint tests to 
verify if the message center indicator module is working properly if a New 
Generation Star (NGS) Tester is not available to monitor PIDs.

 Display Dimming Test 

The following test displays the status of the dimming value sent to the 
message center indicator module over the J1850 communication network by the 
steering column/ignition/lighting control module, as well as the internal 
dimming level set by the message center indicator module.

To sequence through the different message center indicator module 
dimming levels, press the VEHICLE SETTINGS button to increase the VFD dimming 
level, and the TRIP ODO button to decrease the VFD dimming level.

To monitor dimming levels, rotate the instrument panel lamp dimming 
control wheel.

The SCP value displayed indicates the vehicle dimming setting commanded 
by the steering column/ignition/lighting control module.

When the SCP level changes, the message center indicator module will 
immediately change the VFD dimming level to the one that corresponds to the 
steering column/ignition/lighting control module commanded SCP level. Note 
that the message center indicator module illumination brightness will vary in 
response to the SCP/VFD brightness level commanded.

These tests can be used with the pinpoint tests to verify if the 
message center indicator module is working properly if a New Generation Star 
(NGS) Tester is not available to monitor PID

 Inspection and Verification 

Verify the customer's concern by observing the indicators to determine 
if they are operating properly with the ignition switch: 

in RUN without the engine running.

in START before the ignition switch is released.

in RUN with the engine running.

Inspect to determine if any of the following electrical concerns apply: 

 Visual Inspection Chart

Electrical

Fuse junction panel Fuse 28 (10A) or Fuse 5 (10A).

Circuit wiring.

Switches or sensors.

If the inspection reveals obvious concern(s) that can be readily 
identified, service as required.

If the concern remains after the inspection, connect the Rotunda New 
Generation Star (NGS) Tester to the data link connector (DLC) located beneath 
the instrument panel to perform the DATA LINK DIAGNOSTIC TEST; refer to Section 418-00 
. If the New Generation Star (NGS) 
Tester responds with NO RESPONSE/NOT EQUIPPED for the driver seat module or 
message center indicator module, go to Pinpoint Test A 
 for the driver seat 
module, or Pinpoint Test B 
 for the 
message center indicator module. If the 
DATA LINK DIAGNOSTIC TEST is passed for the driver seat module and message 
center indicator module, retrieve continuous diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs) 
and execute Self Test Diagnostics for driver seat module; refer to Section 418-00 
.

If self test is passed and no diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs) are 
retrieved, go the the Symptom Chart 
 to continue diagnostics.

If diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs) are retrieved, go to the Driver Seat 
Module Diagnostic Trouble Code (DTC) Index to continue diagnostics.

If the driver seat module or message center indicator module cannot be 
accessed by the New Generation Star (NGS) Tester, go to Pinpoint Test A 
 for a 
driver seat module, or Pinpoint Test B 
 for the 
message center indicator module.

Section 414-00: Electrical Power Supply System—General Information

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Charging System

The charging system includes:

[FIGURE: AJ0089A.gif]

Item

Part Number

Description

1

10300

Generator

2

10655

Battery

3

14301

Battery Cable

4

10316

Voltage Regulator

The generator (GEN) (10346):

bolts to the cylinder blocks (6010).

is driven by an automatically tensioned drive belt (8620).

is an internal fan and voltage regulator type.

The voltage regulator (VR) (10316):

is housed in the generator.

adjusts generator output.

is serviced with generator removed.

The battery (10655):

is a sealed design with two vents to release gases.

is a 12-volt, direct-current, negative-ground design.

functions as engine cranking power source, a voltage stabilizer for the 
electrical system and a temporary power source when power demands exceed 
generator output.

can by recycled.

The charge indicator:

is located on the instrument panel.

displays charging system status.

Associated wiring:

provides electrical paths to related components.

 Inspection and Verification 

 WARNING: KEEP OUT OF THE REACH OF CHILDREN. BATTERIES (10655) CONTAIN SULFURIC 
ACID. AVOID CONTACT WITH SKIN, EYES, OR CLOTHING. ALSO, SHIELD YOUR EYES WHEN 
WORKING NEAR THE BATTERY TO PROTECT AGAINST POSSIBLE SPLASHING OF THE ACID 
SOLUTION. IN CASE OF ACID CONTACT WITH SKIN OR EYES, FLUSH IMMEDIATELY WITH 
WATER FOR A MINIMUM OF 15 MINUTES AND GET PROMPT MEDICAL ATTENTION. IF ACID IS 
SWALLOWED, CALL A PHYSICIAN IMMEDIATELY. 

 WARNING: BATTERIES NORMALLY PRODUCE EXPLOSIVE GASES WHICH CAN CAUSE PERSONAL 
INJURY. THEREFORE, DO NOT ALLOW FLAMES, SPARKS OR LIGHTED SUBSTANCES TO COME 
NEAR THE BATTERY. WHEN CHARGING OR WORKING NEAR A BATTERY, ALWAYS SHIELD YOUR 
FACE AND PROTECT YOUR EYES. ALWAYS PROVIDE VENTILATION. 

 WARNING: WHEN LIFTING A PLASTIC-CASED BATTERY, EXCESSIVE PRESSURE ON THE END 
WALLS COULD CAUSE ACID TO SPEW THROUGH THE VENT CAPS, RESULTING IN PERSONAL 
INJURY, DAMAGE TO THE VEHICLE OR BATTERY. LIFT WITH A BATTERY CARRIER OR WITH 
YOUR HANDS ON OPPOSITE CORNERS. 

Verify the customer's concern by operating the engine to duplicate the 
concern.

Inspect to determine if one of the following mechanical or electrical 
concerns apply:

 Visual Inspection Chart

Mechanical

Electrical

Before attempting to test a battery, it is important to give it a
thorough examination to determine if it has been damaged.

Batteries are tested to determine the state of charge and ability to
crank an engine. The result of these tests is to show that the battery is
either good, needs recharging, or must be replaced.

Preliminary checks to the charging system should be made regardless of
the fault condition. These checks include:

Check the fuses/fuse links to the generator to make sure that they are
not burned or damaged. This condition, resulting in an open circuit or high
resistance, can cause erratic or intermittent charging system concerns.

Check battery posts and cable terminals for clean and tight
connections. Clean the posts and the cables to make sure electrical contact is
good.

Check for secure connections at the generator output and engine ground.
Also check connection at load distribution point.

Check generator drive belt for proper tension and no slip between
generator pulley and drive belt. Refer to Section 303-05 
.

Check the battery for full charge; refer to the procedure in this
section.

Before performing the charging system tests on the vehicle, note the
conditions such as: slow cranking, discharged battery, charge indicator lamp
stays on with the engine running, charge indicator lamp does not illuminate
with the ignition switch in RUN and the engine not running, etc. This
information will aid in isolating the part of the system causing the symptom.

When a relatively new battery is discharged, test for current drain.
The following are some of the most common current drain sources:

Glove compartment lamp stays on with the door closed.

Engine compartment lamp stays on constantly.

License plate lamp or interior lamp stays on constantly.

Other electronic component malfunctions.

If the inspection reveals obvious concern(s) that can be readily 
identified, service as required.

If the concern(s) remains after the inspection, determine the 
symptom(s) and go to the Symptom Chart.

 Pinpoint Tests 

 CAUTION: Do not make jumper connections except as directed. Improper connections 
may damage the voltage regulator (VR) (10316) or fuses/fuse links. 

 NOTE: All voltage measurements are referenced to the negative (-) battery 
post unless otherwise specified.

 NOTE: All "ignition switch ON" measurements are made with the engine NOT 
running unless directed to "START ENGINE."

 NOTE: When the battery has been disconnected and reconnected, some abnormal 
drive symptoms may occur while the powertrain control module (PCM) (12A650) 
relearns its adaptive strategy. The vehicle may need to be driven 16 km (10 
miles) or more to relearn the strategy.

Section 414-00: Electrical Power Supply System—General Information

1997 Mark VIII Workshop Manual

GENERAL PROCEDURES

Battery Charging

 WARNING: HYDROGEN AND OXYGEN GASES ARE PRODUCED DURING NORMAL BATTERY OPERATION. 
THIS GAS MIXTURE CAN EXPLODE IF FLAMES, SPARKS OR LIGHTED TOBACCO ARE BROUGHT 
NEAR THE BATTERY. WHEN CHARGING OR USING THE BATTERY IN AN ENCLOSED SPACE, 
ALWAYS PROVIDE VENTILATION AND SHIELD YOUR FACE AND EYES. 

 WARNING: BATTERIES CONTAIN SULFURIC ACID. AVOID CONTACT WITH SKIN OR EYES. ALSO, 
SHIELD YOUR EYES WHEN WORKING NEAR THE BATTERY TO PROTECT AGAINST POSSIBLE 
SPLASHING OF THE ACID SOLUTION. IN CASE OF ACID CONTACT WITH SKIN, EYES, OR 
CLOTHING, FLUSH IMMEDIATELY WITH WATER FOR A PERIOD OF 15 MINUTES AND GET 
PROMPT MEDICAL ATTENTION. IF ACID IS SWALLOWED, CALL PHYSICIAN IMMEDIATELY. 

 WARNING: WEAR SAFETY GLASSES. BATTERY CHARGING CAN BE DANGEROUS. WHILE BEING 
CHARGED, THE BATTERY PRODUCES A POTENTIALLY EXPLOSIVE MIXTURE OF HYDROGEN AND 
OXYGEN GASES. KEEP SPARKS, FLAMES AND LIGHTED CIGARETTES AWAY FROM BATTERIES. 
IN CASE OF ACID CONTACT WITH SKIN, EYES OR CLOTHING, FLUSH IMMEDIATELY WITH 
LARGE AMOUNTS OF WATER. GET MEDICAL ATTENTION. 

 CAUTION: Keep the battery and surrounding parts, particularly the top, clean and 
dry. If electrolyte is evident on the top of the battery, clean it off 
immediately. Even a weak electrolyte quickly attacks and corrodes the cable 
connections, battery hold down clamp (10718) and the battery ground cable 
(14301). Use a rag soaked in a weak solution of water and ammonia to 
counteract the action of spilled electrolyte. 

 CAUTION: If excessive gassing or electrolyte spewing occurs during the charge, 
discontinue charging. The battery has reached a serviceable charge. If the 
battery will not accept at least 5 amps after 20 minutes of charging, replace 
the battery. 

Before recharging a discharged battery, inspect and service the 
following conditions, if they exist:

Loose drive belt; refer to Section 303-05 
.

Pinched or grounded generator voltage regulator wiring.

Loose connections of the generator voltage regulator wiring at the 
generator or the voltage regulator.

Loose or corroded connections at the battery, starter motor cutout 
relay (11433) or engine (6007).

Excessive battery drain due to luggage compartment lamp, glove 
compartment lamp or interior lamps remaining energized.

Allow batteries to warm up to approximately 5°C (41°F) before 
charging. This may require four to eight hours at room temperature depending 
on the initial temperature and battery size.

A battery which has been completely discharged may be slow to accept a 
charge initially and in some cases may not accept a charge at the normal 
charger setting. When batteries are in this condition, charging can be started 
by use of the dead battery switch on chargers so equipped.

To determine whether a battery is accepting a charge, follow the 
charger manufacturer's instructions for use of the dead battery switch. If the 
switch is a spring-loaded type, it should be held in the ON position for up to 
three minutes.

After releasing the switch and with the charger still on, measure the 
battery voltage. If the voltage is 12 volts or more, the battery is accepting 
a charge and is capable of being recharged. However, it may require up to two 
hours of charging with batteries colder than 5°C (41°F) before the 
charge rate is high enough to show on the charger ammeter. It has been found 
that all non-damaged batteries can be charged by this procedure. If a battery 
cannot be charged by this procedure, it should be replaced.

A rapid recharge procedure has been developed for recharging batteries 
that have passed the Load Test and only need a recharge. This can be due to: 
in-service, no-start battery failures (the vehicle will not crank due to a low 
state of charge), or the battery was discharged in the vehicle due to key-off 
loads. Refer to the Load Test 
 procedure in this section.

The battery can be rapidly recharged by using either of the following 
methods:

Perform a 2-hour charge using a 20A constant current (manual setting on 
charger).

Perform a 2-hour charge using a constant potential (automatic setting 
on charger).

Battery

 Removal 

 WARNING: KEEP OUT OF THE REACH OF CHILDREN. BATTERIES (10655) CONTAIN SULFURIC 
ACID. AVOID CONTACT WITH SKIN, EYES, OR CLOTHING. ALSO, SHIELD YOUR EYES WHEN 
WORKING NEAR THE BATTERY TO PROTECT AGAINST POSSIBLE SPLASHING OF THE ACID 
SOLUTION. IN CASE OF ACID CONTACT WITH SKIN OR EYES, FLUSH IMMEDIATELY WITH 
WATER FOR A MINIMUM OF 15 MINUTES AND GET PROMPT MEDICAL ATTENTION. IF ACID IS 
SWALLOWED, CALL A PHYSICIAN IMMEDIATELY. 

 WARNING: BATTERIES NORMALLY PRODUCE EXPLOSIVE GASES WHICH CAN CAUSE PERSONAL 
INJURY. THEREFORE, DO NOT ALLOW FLAMES, SPARKS OR LIGHTED SUBSTANCES TO COME 
NEAR THE BATTERY. WHEN CHARGING OR WORKING NEAR A BATTERY, ALWAYS SHIELD YOUR 
FACE AND PROTECT YOUR EYES. ALWAYS PROVIDE VENTILATION. 

 WARNING: THE BACKUP POWER SUPPLY ENERGY MUST BE DEPLETED BEFORE ANY AIR BAG 
COMPONENT SERVICE IS PERFORMED. TO DEPLETE BACKUP POWER SUPPLY ENERGY, FIRST 
DISCONNECT THE BATTERY GROUND CABLE, THEN DISCONNECT THE POSITIVE BATTERY 
CABLE AND WAIT ONE MINUTE TO AVOID ACCIDENTAL DEPLOYMENT AND POSSIBLE PERSONAL 
INJURY.

Section 415-00: In-Vehicle Entertainment System—General Information

1997 Mark VIII Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Audio System

The Mark VIII is equipped with a Premium Audio System or it can be 
upgraded with JBL® components. Both systems can support the Premium 
Analog Cassette Radio Chassis or the Digital Audio Compact Disc Radio Chassis.

 Premium 

The Premium sound system, which is standard on the Mark VIII, consists 
of the following features:

a Premium Analog Cassette Radio Chassis or a Digital Audio Compact Disc 
Radio Chassis 

four radio speakers (two premium front door speakers and two premium 
quarter trim panel-mounted speakers)

a premium radio amplifier

 JBL® 

The JBL® sound system consists of the following features:

a Premium Analog Cassette Radio Chassis or a Digital Audio Compact Disc 
Radio Chassis 

eight radio speakers (a JBL® woofer and a JBL® tweeter 
in each of the front doors and in the quarter trim panels)

a JBL® radio amplifier

an optional luggage compartment-mounted 10-disc digital audio compact 
disc changer

Component Location

[FIGURE: AK0992B.gif]

 Radio Chassis 

Two different radio chassis are possible; the Premium Analog Cassette 
Radio Chassis or the Digital Audio Compact Disc Radio Chassis. The radio 
chassis have the following features:

The radio chassis are interchangeable in either the premium or 
JBL® upgrade audio system.

The Premium Analog Cassette Radio Chassis has remote compact disc 
player control functions even if the vehicle is not equipped with a remote 
compact disc changer.

Both the Digital Audio Compact Disc Radio Chassis and the Premium 
Analog Cassette Radio Chassis will diagnose and display error messages.

 Radio Amplifier 

The radio amplifier (18B849) is located on the relay panel (14B120) 
along with the mobile telephone transceiver (19A387) (if equipped). The relay 
panel is attached to the underside of the package tray in the luggage 
compartment. The radio amplifier has the following features:

Both the premium and JBL® amplifiers are in operation and are 
part of the audio system circuit at all times.

The premium amplifier has four separate output channels to four speakers.

The JBL® amplifier has four separate output channels to four 
JBL® tweeters and two separate output channels to four JBL® 
woofers.

If any of the speaker leads shorts to ground, the amplifier will shut 
down until the short is serviced.

 10-Disc Digital Audio Compact Disc Changer 

The digital audio compact disc changer is located in the luggage 
compartment and is only available with the JBL® upgrade. The digital 
audio compact disc changer has the following features:

separate audio signal feeds to the radio chassis

control communication with the radio chassis via the audio control 
protocol (ACP) multiplex network

heat-protection circuitry to shut down and protect the laser diode. An 
error message will be displayed.

 Antenna 

The AM and FM antennas are concealed on the rear window glass and have 
the following features:

The rear window defroster grid also serves as the AM antenna.

The FM antenna is a separate on-glass tracing above the defroster grid.

The radio antenna lead in cable (18812) connects the FM antenna tracing 
to the radio antenna isolator (18K891).

The FM antenna tracing and terminal lug can be serviced in the same 
manner as the rear window defroster grid.

 Radio Antenna Isolator 

The radio antenna isolator is mounted on top of the rear package tray 
under the trim cover and has the following features:

It isolates the AM antenna signal from the rear window defroster current.

The defroster grid leads are part of the radio antenna isolator.

Both AM and FM signals are conducted from the radio antenna isolator to 
the radio chassis (18806) over a single coaxial cable.

Radio Frequency Interference Suppression Equipment

 Radio Ignition Interference Capacitors 

There are two radio ignition interference capacitors (18801) mounted on 
the engine. They are located on the rear of the cylinder heads and attached 
with a single screw.

 Radio Frequency Interference Suppression Bond Assembly 

One end of the radio frequency interference suppression bond (19A095) 
(ground strap) is attached with a nut to the right engine mount stud. The 
other end is attached to the side of the frame with a screw.

 Hood Bonding Straps 

The hood bonding straps are part of the hood hinges and are not 
available as a separate component.

1997 Mark VIII

Section 417-01: Exterior Lighting

1997 Mark VIII Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Headlamps

 Aerodynamic 

The low beam headlamps are high intensity display (HID) lighting. The 
steering column/ignition/lighting control module controls the power source to 
the individual headlamp ballast's depending on the position of the autolamp 
switch, the headlamp switch (11654) and the dimmer switch.

Power for both headlamp ballasts is constantly supplied to the steering 
column/ignition/lighting control module through a 60A maxifuse in the power 
distribution box and harness (14516) and through fuse junction panel Fuse 19 
(10A) for the LH ballast and Fuse 25 (10A) for the RH ballast.

The steering column/ignition/lighting control module will supply power 
to the LH and RH headlamp ballasts if the headlamp switch is in the low beam 
position and the headlamp switch is turned on or the autolamp system is 
operating.

On late production vehicles the low beam headlamp HID bulb and ballast
are serviced separately. These vehicles have an orange warning label
on the connector between the ballast and the low beam headlamp bulb.
On earlier production vehicles there is no orange warning label on
the connector between the ballast and the low beam bulb. The
connector used on these earlier production vehicles cannot be
disconnected and the ballast and the headlamp assembly are serviced
as an assembly.

The steering column/ignition/lighting control module also monitors the 
windshield wiper operation. When the windshield wipers are turned to low or 
high speed, the steering column/ignition/lighting control module will turn on 
the low beam headlamps. If the
windshield wipers are turned off, the headlamps 
will be turned off unless autolamps are operating. The steering 
column/ignition/lighting control module uses a timing feature to detect 
intermittent wiper mode and will not turn on the headlamps in this mode. This 
function can be disabled through the Vehicle Settings on the message center 
indicator module.

The high beam headlamps are halogen bulbs. The high beam headlamps are 
powered by the high beam relay located in the power distribution box and 
harness. The high beam relay is activated by the steering 
column/ignition/lighting control module which grounds the high beam relay coil 
when the dimmer switch is pulled towards the steering wheel (3600) . The first 
dimmer switch detent is flash-to-pass position and will illuminate the high 
beams until released. The second dimmer switch detent position is the high 
beam position and will illuminate the high beams until the dimmer switch is 
pulled to this position again.

The steering column/ignition/lighting control module also controls the 
battery saver feature. If the headlamps are left on, the battery saver feature 
will automatically turn the headlamps off if:

the ignition switch is turned to OFF.

the headlamp switch is in the HEAD position.

ten minutes expire since the last input.

The steering column/ignition/lighting control module battery saver 
function will also turn the interior demand lighting off after 30 minutes 
expire. Refer to Section 417-02 
 for more information.

 Headlamp Delay System - Autolamp 

The autolamp system:

provides light sensitive ON-OFF control of exterior lamps.

allows exterior lamps to remain lit for up to three minutes upon 
exiting the vehicle.

is controlled by light sensor amplifier (13A018), located under the 
finish panel at the top right corner of the instrument panel (04320), and 
steering column/ignition/lighting control module.

ON-OFF control and time delay adjustment is controlled by the headlamp 
switch. Turn headlamp switch to AUTOLAMP position, then adjust time from 
minimum to maximum delay.

the current time delay period is displayed in the message center.

 Daytime Running Lamps 

Refer to Section 417-04 
.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Headlamp Switch

Controls parking lamps, headlamps and autolamp functions.

Chime will sound if headlamp switch (11654) is in PARK or HEAD position 
and driver door is opened.

 Panel Dim Switch 

Controls instrument panel illumination intensity by rotating thumbwheel.

Rotating thumbwheel to the full up position turns ON interior lamps.

Section 417-01: Exterior Lighting

1997 Mark VIII Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Turn Signal and Hazard Lamps

The turn signal system consists of:

multi-function switch (13K359).

steering column/ignition/lighting control module.

redundant directional flashers in the outside rear view mirrors.

turn signal bulbs and circuitry.

The multi-function switch is an integrated switch design. When the 
multi-function switch is activated in either direction, or the hazard switch 
is engaged, a request is made from the multi-function switch to the steering 
column/ignition/lighting control module to flash the appropriate turn signal 
lamps, mirror indicators and turn signal indicators in the instrument cluster. 
The instrument cluster is equipped with a relay to provide an audible click 
anytime one or both of the indicators illuminates.

 Inspection and Verification 

 NOTE: If the headlamp switch loses power, the steering 
column/ignition/lighting control module will automatically default to the 
autolamp mode. With the ignition switch in RUN, the autolamp function will 
turn on the exterior lamps and the instrument panel lighting depending on the 
input of the light sensor amplifier as in normal operation, however the exit 
delay will be defaulted to the full three minutes.
Verify the customer's concern by operating the headlamp/autolamp system 
to duplicate the condition.

Inspect to determine if one of the following electrical concerns apply:

 Visual Inspection Chart

Electrical

Circuitry open/shorted.

Damaged light sensor amplifier.

Damaged power distribution box Fuse 2 (15A), fuse junction panel Fuse
19 (10A), 26 (15A), 1 (10A), 25 (10A), 13 (15A), 7 (15A), 12 (15A) and 31 (10A).

Damaged headlamp switch.

Burned-out bulb.

If the inspection reveals obvious concern(s) that can be readily 
identified, service as required.

If the concern remains after inspection, connect the Rotunda New 
Generation Star (NGS) Tester to the data link connector (DLC) located beneath 
the instrument panel to perform DATA LINK DIAGNOSTIC TEST; refer to Section 418-00 
. If the New Generation Star (NGS) 
Tester responds with NO RESPONSE/NOT EQUIPPED for Steering 
Column/Ignition/Lighting Control Module, go to Pinpoint Test AB 
. If the DATA 
LINK DIAGNOSTIC TEST is passed for the Steering Column/Ignition/Lighting 
Control Module, retrieve continuous diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs) and 
execute Self Test Diagnostics for Steering Column/Ignition/Lighting Control 
Module; refer to Section 418-00 
.

If self test is passed and no diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs) are 
retrieved, go to the Symptom Chart 
 to continue diagnostics.

If diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs) are retrieved, go to the Steering 
Column/Ignition/Lighting Control Module Diagnostic Trouble Code (DTC) Index to 
continue diagnostics.

If the Steering Column/Ignition/Lighting Control Module cannot be 
accessed by the New Generation Star (NGS) tester, go to Pinpoint Test AB 
.

 Symptom Chart—Backup Lamps 

 BACKUP LAMPS 

Condition

Possible Source

Action

Backup Lamps Inoperative

Circuitry open/shorted.

Damaged transmission range sensor.

Open fuse.

GO to Pinpoint Test FA .

Individual Backup Lamp Inoperative

Supply circuit open.

Burned out miniature bulb.

Ground circuit open.

SERVICE as required.

Backup Lamps On Continuously

Circuitry open/shorted.

Damaged transmission range sensor.

GO to Pinpoint Test FB .

1997 Mark VIII Workshop Manual

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Headlamp Assembly — Without Serviceable Low Beam Headlamp Bulb

 Removal 

 WARNING: THE REPLACEABLE HALOGEN HEADLAMP BULB CONTAINS GAS UNDER PRESSURE. THE 
BULB MAY SHATTER IF THE GLASS ENVELOPE IS SCRATCHED OR IF THE BULB IS DROPPED. 
GRASP BULB ONLY BY ITS PLASTIC BASE. AVOID TOUCHING GLASS ENVELOPE. KEEP BULB 
OUT OF REACH OF CHILDREN. 

Disconnect the battery ground cable. Refer to Section 414-01 
.

Remove the radiator upper sight shield (8C291).

[FIGURE: AN0624A.gif]

Remove the retaining screw from headlamp (13008).

[FIGURE: AK0427A.gif]

Remove the mounting bolts from headlamp.

[FIGURE: AK0428A.gif]

Remove headlamp assembly.

Pull headlamp assembly forward and disconnect high beam harness.

Disconnect turn signal harness.

Disconnect cornering lamp harness.

Disconnect the side marker lamp and harness.

Cut wire between burner assembly and ballast.

Remove headlamp assembly.

[FIGURE: AK0429B.gif]

[FIGURE: AK1325A.gif]

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Headlamp Bulb, Low Beam—With Serviceable Low Beam Headlamp Bulbs

 Removal 

 WARNING: THE REPLACEABLE HALOGEN HEADLAMP BULB CONTAINS GAS UNDER PRESSURE. THE 
BULB MAY SHATTER IF THE GLASS ENVELOPE IS SCRATCHED OR IF THE BULB IS DROPPED. 
GRASP BULB ONLY BY ITS PLASTIC BASE. AVOID TOUCHING GLASS ENVELOPE. KEEP BULB 
OUT OF REACH OF CHILDREN. 

Disconnect the battery ground cable. Refer to Section 414-01 
.

Remove the radiator upper sight shield.

[FIGURE: AN0624A.gif]

Remove the retaining screw from the headlamp.

[FIGURE: AK0427A.gif]

Remove the mounting bolts from the headlamp.

[FIGURE: AK0428A.gif]

Remove headlamp assembly.

Pull headlamp assembly forward.

Disconnect turn signal harness.

Disconnect cornering lamp harness.

Disconnect the side marker lamp and harness.

Disconnect the high beam harness connector and the low beam harness to 
the ballast connector located on the grille opening panel by the radiator 
support bracket.

Remove headlamp assembly.

[FIGURE: AK1402A.gif]

With headlamp assembly on bench:

Remove the tape holding the low beam wires and the high beam wires 
together at the harness connectors.

Remove the low beam wire from the clip on the top of the headlamp 
assembly.

Locate the low beam headlamp bulb cover.

[FIGURE: AK1403A.gif]

Remove the low beam headlamp housing cover.

Twist the low beam headlamp housing cover counterclockwise to the 
unlock position.

Pull the low beam headlamp housing cover backwards to expose the 
headlamp bulb retaining nuts.

[FIGURE: AK1404A.gif]

Remove the low beam headlamp retaining nuts.

[FIGURE: AK1441A.gif]

Remove the low beam headlamp bulb assembly.

[FIGURE: AK1406A.gif]

Slide the vehicle headlamp aiming device (VHAD) over the low beam 
headlamp assembly and wiring and remove.

[FIGURE: AK1407A.gif]

Twist headlamp housing cover harness seal counterclockwise to unlock 
and separate low beam headlamp housing cover and low beam headlamp assembly.

[FIGURE: AK1408A.gif]

 Installation 

Install the low beam headlamp housing cover.

Pull the wire harness through the housing cover.

Twist the harness seal clockwise to lock into place.

[FIGURE: AK1410A.gif]

Slip the vehicle headlamp aiming device (VHAD) over the low beam 
headlamp wiring and slide onto the low beam headlamp assembly.

[FIGURE: AK1411A.gif]

Install the low beam headlamp bulb.

[FIGURE: AK1405A.gif]

Line up tabs on low beam headlamp retaining cover, twist retainer 
clockwise to lock position.

[FIGURE: AK1412A.gif]

Install the headlamp.

Install the low beam headlamp wire into the clip on the top of the 
headlamp assembly.

Tape the low beam and the high beam headlamp wires together at the 
harness connectors.

Connect the turn signal harness.

Connect the cornering lamp harness.

Connect the side marker harness.

Route the high beam and the low beam headlamp wiring through radiator 
grille opening panel and connect low beam headlamp and high beam headlamp 
connectors. Install headlamp assembly in place.

[FIGURE: AK1413A.gif]

Install the headlamp mounting bolts.

[FIGURE: AK1325A.gif]

Install the headlamp retaining screw.

[FIGURE: AK1434A.gif]

Follow the headlamp aiming procedure as described in General Procedures 
to verify that the vehicle is sitting level.

Adjust the vertical aim adjustment.

Install the radiator upper sight shield.

[FIGURE: AN0625A.gif]

Connect the battery ground cable. Refer to Section 414-01 
.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Courtesy Lamps

Component Locations

[FIGURE: AK0001A.gif]

Item

Part Number

Description

1

—

Steering Column/Ignition/Lighting (SCIL) Control Module

2

10E846

Instrument Panel Lamp Dimmer Control

3

—

Dome/Map Combination Lamp

4

17682

Outside Rear View Mirror Ground Illumination

5

13713

Interior Lamp Switch

6

—

Courtesy/Reading Lamps

Courtesy lamps illuminate when any door is opened or when the 
instrument panel lamp dimmer control (10E846) is in the detented UP position. 
The theater lighting feature gradually increases or decreases courtesy lamp 
intensity when any door is opened and closed. The courtesy lamps are 
controlled by the steering column/ignition/lighting (SCIL) control module. 
Courtesy lamps include:

driver and passenger door courtesy lamps.

dome/map combination lamp.

courtesy reading lamp.

================================================================================
PAGE 4885
================================================================================
1997 Mark VIII

Section 417-02: Interior Lighting

1997 Mark VIII Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Illuminated Entry

The illuminated entry function is controlled by the steering 
column/ignition/lighting (SCIL) control module. The control module will 
illuminate the courtesy lamps when:

any switch on the keyless entry keypad (14A626) is pressed.

the unlock switch on the keyless entry remote transmitter (15K601) is 
pressed.

================================================================================
PAGE 4886
================================================================================
1997 Mark VIII

Section 417-02: Interior Lighting

1997 Mark VIII Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Battery Saver

The battery saver function prevents excessive battery drain from loads 
inadvertently left on when the ignition switch is in the OFF position. The 
steering column/ignition/lighting (SCIL) control module interrupts power to:

courtesy lamps after ten minutes.

demand lighting after thirty minutes.

Demand lighting includes:

map lamps.

reading lamps.

visor mirror lamps.

glove compartment lamp.

luggage compartment lamp (15702).

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Courtesy Lamps and Illuminated Entry

 Electrical Schematic Reference(s) 

Refer to Electrical and Vacuum Troubleshooting Manual, Cell 89 , Courtesy Lamps for schematic and connector information. 

Refer to Electrical and Vacuum Troubleshooting Manual, Cell 58 , Lighting Control Module for schematic and connector information.

Refer to Electrical and Vacuum Troubleshooting Manual, Cell 71 , Instrument Illumination for schematic and connector information. 

 Special Service Tool(s) 

[FIGURE: ST1217A.gif]

New Generation Star (NGS) Tester

007-00500 or equivalent

[FIGURE: ST1137A.gif]

73 Digital Multimeter

105-R0051

 Inspection and Verification 

 NOTE: If the headlamp switch loses power, the steering 
column/ignition/lighting control module will automatically default to the 
autolamp mode. With the ignition switch in RUN, the autolamp function will 
turn on the exterior lamps and the instrument panel lighting depending on the 
input of the light sensor amplifier as in normal operation, however the exit 
delay will be defaulted to the full three minutes.
Verify the customer's concern by operating the courtesy lamps and 
illuminated entry to duplicate the condition.

Inspect to determine if one of the following mechanical or electrical 
concerns apply: 

 Visual Inspection Chart

Mechanical

Electrical

Damaged interior lamps.

Damaged switches.

Stuck switches.

Open fuse junction panel Fuse 26 (15A), Fuse 5 (10A), Fuse 1 (10A) or
Fuse 41 (10A).

Damaged miniature bulbs.

Circuitry open/shorted.

Connectors damaged/corroded.

Damaged driver door module or steering column/ignition/lighting control
module.

If the inspection reveals obvious concern(s) that can be readily 
identified, service as required.

If the concern remains after the inspection, connect the Rotunda New 
Generation Star (NGS) Tester to the data link connector (DLC) located beneath 
the instrument panel to perform DATA LINK DIAGNOSTIC TEST; refer to Section 418-00 
. If the NGS responds with NO 
RESPONSE/NOT EQUIPPED for the steering column/ignition/lighting control 
module, go to Pinpoint Test AA 
. If the NGS responds with NO RESPONSE/NOT 
EQUIPPED for the driver door module, go to Pinpoint Test AB 
. If the DATA LINK 
DIAGNOSTIC TEST is passed for the steering column/ignition/lighting control 
module and driver door module, retrieve continuous diagnostic trouble codes 
(DTCs) and execute Self Test Diagnostics for steering column/ignition/lighting 
control module and driver door module; refer to Section 418-00 
.

If self test is passed and no diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs) are 
retrieved, go to the Symptom Chart 
 to continue diagnostics.

If DTCs are retrieved for the steering column/ignition/lighting control 
module, go to the Steering Column/Ignition/Lighting Control Module Diagnostic 
Trouble Code (DTC) Index to continue diagnostics. If DTCs are retrieved for 
the driver door module, go to the Driver Door Module Diagnostic Trouble Code 
(DTC) Index to continue diagnostics.

If the steering column/ignition/lighting control module cannot be 
accessed by the NGS tester, go to Pinpoint Test AA 
. If the driver door module 
cannot be accessed by the NGS tester, go to Pinpoint Test AB 
.

Section 417-04: Daytime Running Lamps

1997 Mark VIII Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Daytime Running Lamp (DRL) System

Component Location

[FIGURE: AK0827B.gif]

Item

Part Number

Description

1

15A272

Daytime Running Lamps Control

The daytime running lamp (DRL) system is designed to turn the high-beam 
headlamps (13008) ON, with a reduced light output and without illuminating the 
high-beam indicator in the hybrid electronic instrument cluster, when the 
following conditions are met:

The ignition switch is in the RUN position.

The park brake is fully released.

The headlamp switch (11654) is in the OFF or PARK lamp position.

Transmission is not in the PARK position.

 NOTE: Vehicle is equipped with an autolamp system. The DRL system is active 
until the autolamp system turns on the headlamps.

The DRL system is required by the Canadian government for the vehicles 
sold in Canada. 

The DRL uses a daytime running lamps control (15A272) module.

 WARNING: DRL CONTROL MODULE GETS VERY HOT DURING OPERATION. BE SURE MODULE HAS 
COOLED BEFORE HANDLING IT OR PERSONAL INJURY MAY OCCUR.

instrument cluster for proper operation.

 to service headlamp concerns 
before checking the daytime running lamps.

Turn the ignition switch to RUN.

Check for the high beam headlamps ON at reduced intensity.

 Visual Inspection Chart

The J1850 communication network provides:

the ability for module-to-module communication by sharing required 
inputs and outputs instead of each component having an input or output wired 
directly to or from each affected module.

a common link for communication to an off-board tester through the data 
link connector (DLC) located under the instrument panel to the right of the 
steering column.

Ten micro-processor based subsystems are included in this network to 
control:

powertrain systems

chassis systems

body electrical systems

The J1850 bus between these subsystems and the data link connector 
(DLC) consist of an unshielded twisted pair of wires:

Circuit 914 (T/O) Bus+

Circuit 915 (PK/LB) Bus-

 Fault Tolerance 

The J1850 communication network will remain operational in the event:

one circuit is severed.

one circuit is shorted to ground.

one circuit is shorted to battery positive (B+) voltage.

a termination resistor is lost within a module.

one or more modules fail internally or lose power or ground.

Any of these conditions will be detected and reported to the off-board 
tester during diagnostics in the form of a diagnostic trouble code (DTC).

 Purpose 

The information within this section is designed to diagnose J1850 
communication network concerns. These concerns may:

affect normal functional operations of the vehicle.

be directly related to customer concerns.

be undetectable except during diagnostics.

To properly diagnose a network concern, follow the diagnostic procedure 
described in this section in the order presented.

 Module Identification 

Modules included on this J1850 communication network include:

Anti-Lock Brake System (ABS) Control Module

located under the battery tray (10732) in the lower LH side of the 
engine compartment.

a failed anti-lock brake control module may cause a no communication 
condition on J1850 communication network.

if communication to the anti-lock brake control module fails, refer to 
Section 206-09 for No Communication Testing.

Portable Support Electronics - Cellular Phone Module (CPM)

located in the luggage compartment, beneath the rear package shelf.

if communication to the portable support electronics fails, refer to 
Section 419-08 for No Communication testing.

Driver Door Module

located inside driver door behind driver front door trim panel (23942) .

if communication to the driver door module fails, refer to Section 501-14 
 for No Communication testing.

Driver Seat Module

located under the driver seat.

if communication to the driver seat module fails, refer to Section 412-00 
 for No Communication testing.

Electronic Automatic Temperature Control (EATC)

located on the A/C evaporator core housing (19A553) on the passenger 
side of the vehicle.

loss of communication to electronic automatic temperature control may 
result in degraded automatic temperature control.

if communication to the electronic automatic temperature control module 
is lost, refer to Section 412-00 
 for No Communication testing.

Hybrid Electronic Instrument Cluster

located in the instrument panel (04320).

if communication to the hybrid electronic instrument cluster fails, 
refer to Section 413-01 
 for No Communication testing.

Message Center Indicator Module

located in the center of the instrument panel.

if communication to the message center indicator module fails, refer to Section 413-08A 
 for No Communication testing.

Powertrain Control Module (PCM)

located under the instrument panel to left of the steering column.

a failure of the communication network to the powertrain control module 
(PCM) (12A650) may result in a no start condition.

if communication to the powertrain control module fails, refer to Communication Systems
Diagnostics 
 in this section.

Steering Column/Ignition/Lighting Control Module

located behind the instrument panel to right of the glove compartment.

if communication to the steering column/ignition/lighting control 
module fails, refer to Section 417-01 
 for No Communication Testing.

Variable Load Control Module

located behind the RH front fender in front of wheel opening.

does not store DTCs. Any DTCs generated by the variable load control 
module are stored by and retrieved from the powertrain control module.

if communication to the variable load control module fails, refer to Communication Systems
Diagnostics 
 in this section.

The ISO 9141 Communication Link:

consists of a single wire, Circuit 70 (LB/W)

provides a common link for communication to an off-board tester through 
the data link connector (DLC) located under the instrument panel to the right 
of the steering column.

 DOES NOT allow module-to-module communications.

The micro-processor based subsystem included on this network is:

passenger seat module.

 Fault Tolerance 

The ISO 9141 communication link will fail if any of the following occur:

Circuit 70 (LB/W) is shorted to ground.

Circuit 70 (LB/W) is shorted to battery positive voltage B+.

the module loses power or ground supply.

a module failure shorts the ISO 9141 communication link internally.

 Purpose 

The information within this section is designed to diagnose ISO 9141 
communication link concerns. These concerns may:

affect normal functional operations of the vehicle.

be directly related to customer concerns.

be undetectable except during diagnostics.

described in this section in the order presented.

located under the passenger seat.

if communication to the passenger seat module fails, refer to Section 501-10 
 for No Communication testing.

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

New Generation Star (NGS) Tester Usage

 Electrical Schematic Reference(s) 

Refer to Electrical and Vacuum Troubleshooting Manual, Cell 14 , Multiplex Communication Network for schematic and connector information. 

 Special Service Tool(s) 

[FIGURE: ST1217A.gif]

New Generation Star (NGS) Tester

007-00500 or equivalent

 Hookup and Vehicle Selection 

Before any diagnostics can be performed on the communication system, 
use Rotunda New Generation Star Tester to perform the following steps:

Turn the ignition switch to OFF.

Select the appropriate program card for the vehicle.

With the New Generation Star Tester control unit facing away from you, 
insert the program card into the slot on the back. If you insert the card 
incorrectly, the card will not seat and the New Generation Star Tester will 
not work.

Connect the New Generation Star Tester to the data link connector (DLC).

If using an alternate power hook up, plug the power cable into the 
vehicle's cigar lighter socket or into the battery hookup adapter.

Turn ignition switch to RUN position. New Generation Star Tester will 
perform an initialization, which checks the New Generation Star Tester memory 
and verifies that the vehicle interface module matches the program card 
software. If the screen displays an error message, refer to Appendix C of the 
New Generation Star Tester Operator Handbook, System Messages.

Menu item "Vehicle and Engine Selection" is highlighted. Press trigger 
to select.

Rotate dial to menu item "Select New Vehicle Model and Year" and press 
trigger.

Select year, vehicle and appropriate engine by rotating dial to 
highlight the selection, then press trigger to select. If the selected vehicle 
is not displayed on the first row, repeat steps 8 and 9.

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Data Link Diagnostic Test

Section 418-00: Module Communications Network

1997 Mark VIII Workshop Manual

GENERAL PROCEDURES

Communication Circuit Wiring Repair

 NOTE: If either Circuit 914 or Circuit 915 is repaired or replaced without 
following proper repair procedures, the operation of the J1850 Communication 
Network will be degraded.

Circuit 914 and Circuit 915 must be twisted at a rate of 33-40 twists 
per meter anytime replacement of either circuit is required. The twist must be 
within 10 centimeters of any connector termination point.

The conductor for Circuit 914 and Circuit 915 must be No. 20 AWG wire.

Refer to the Electrical and Vacuum Troubleshooting Manual for basic 
wiring repair procedure.

The perimeter anti-theft system provides vehicle protection as follows:

The anti-theft alarm system activates the visual and audio alarms and 
disables the engine if a violation of the locked vehicle occurs.

The anti-theft alarm system is managed by the steering 
column/ignition/lighting control module.

The anti-theft alarm system provides perimeter (unauthorized vehicle 
entry) protection.

The anti-theft alarm system powers up in the same mode as when the 
power was interrupted.

A violation of the perimeter security (sensed through the door ajar 
switches) will sound the horn (13832), flash the headlamps, the parking lamps 
and the courtesy lamps.

The anti-theft alarm system protects the engine compartment through a 
pin switch (located on the RH front fender apron (16054)).

1997 Mark VIII

Section 419-01A: Anti-Theft Warning—Perimeter

1997 Mark VIII Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

System Arming

The perimeter security mode is enabled and disabled passively 
(dedicated to the routine entry and exit steps). The arming mode begins when 
the ignition switch is turned OFF and a door is opened. This starts the 
anti-theft indicator lamp on the indicator lamp module flashing and the system 
begins the arming sequence. The system monitors the door ajar status and the 
door lock status. The system arms 30 seconds after both doors are locked and 
closed. This occurs when the doors are locked using either the power lock 
buttons inside the vehicle, the lock button on the keyless entry remote 
transmitter (15K601) or the keyless entry keypad (14A626).

The arming sequence will cancel if:

any door is opened during the 30-second arming sequence. The system 
will reset automatically upon the door being closed and locked and restart the 
arming sequence.

turning the ignition switch to ACC or RUN.

unlocking the doors with the door lock cylinder, using a keyless entry 
code or the keyless entry remote transmitter.

The system can be armed after being disarmed if the doors are closed, 
and the ignition switch is OFF by:

pressing the keyless entry remote transmitter lock button.

locking the doors with the keyless entry keypad.

Arming will occur 30 seconds after the arming sequence is started.

Once the system is armed, any violation of the protected areas will set 
off the alarm. The hood may remain open without the alarm sounding if the hood 
was open during the entire arming sequence.

Section 419-01A: Anti-Theft Warning—Perimeter

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Disarming an Untriggered System

The system will be disarmed if:

the driver or passenger door is unlocked with the key.

the driver door is unlocked with the keyless entry keypad (14A626).

the driver door is unlocked with the keyless entry remote transmitter 
(15K601).

the ignition switch is turned to ACC or RUN.
